content.family: Certified radius adaptation for strongly monotone variational inequalities

limitations.scope: All variants, with rates restricted to the two linked instantiations.
limitations.statement: No generic complexity theorem is asserted for arbitrary finite certified T. Exact information complexity excludes arithmetic, bit-complexity and numerical model-solving costs.

model_and_interfaces.definitions: For 0<R<=D and epsilon>0, Q_R=L_p R^p/epsilon and L_A(R,epsilon)=1+log(2+D/R+Q_R). kappa_D=L_p D^(p-1)/mu and L_S(mu,delta)=1+log(2+kappa_D+L_p D^p/delta+mu D/delta). All log arguments are dimensionless.
model_and_interfaces.domain_and_norm: Finite-dimensional Euclidean space R^d, d>=1; known nonempty compact convex X with diam(X)<=D, D>0. Norms of vectors are Euclidean and derivative norms are multilinear operator norms. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for every u in X}. No artificial ball replaces X.
model_and_interfaces.information: Public: X,d,p,L_p,D,w,mu,delta and the trial implementation with known constants. Hidden: G beyond queried jets, its unique VI solution zstar, and r_true=||w-zstar||. r_true is analysis-only and never an input or stopping test. A feasible order-p query returns (G,DG,...,D^(p-1)G).
model_and_interfaces.regularity: Fixed integer p>=2 and known L_p>0. G is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X, Lip(D^(p-1)G)<=L_p on X, and <G(x)-G(y),x-y>>=mu||x-y||^2 for x,y in X, mu>0. No continuous pth derivative or separate lower-derivative bounds are required. w belongs to X and delta>0.
model_and_interfaces.residual_interface: A_{alpha,b}(F,x0,R,epsilon), for monotone F in this regularity class, has the promise that some VI solution is within R of x0. With a valid promise it returns (y,n,F(y)) with y in X, genuine n in N_X(y), an already evaluated F(y), and ||F(y)+n||<=epsilon, using at most C_p(1+Q_R^alpha)L_A(R,epsilon)^b original queries. A fixed known implementation constant specifies its interruptible cap. On false promises it may fail but never return unchecked success.
model_and_interfaces.strong_interface: S_{gamma,b}(G,w,mu,delta) is not given r_true and returns an evaluated genuine normal certificate of norm <=delta within C_p[1+(L_p r_true^(p-1)/mu)^gamma]L_S(mu,delta)^b original queries. At r_true=0 the additive constant governs. Constants are fixed, known, instance-independent implementation constants, chosen recursively for the fixed exponents used in the paper.

performance_links.scope_note: Only AdaptiveStrong(RestartTrial(A_{alpha,b})): S_{alpha,b+2}; imported A is an abstract input.

variants.cost: The sum of actual original queries in all attempted trials, including certificate evaluations and descendants. Finite certification alone gives no universal performance rate for arbitrary T.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Original PDF Algorithm 3 p.17; Definition 5.1 p.16.
variants.name: AdaptiveStrong with an abstract finite certified trial
variants.output: Feasible y, genuine n in N_X(y), saved evaluated G(y), and ||G(y)+n||<=delta; or Failure only when the trial contract or instance assumptions do not ensure success.
variants.query_and_update: Run T(G,w,mu,R,delta) from w. If its verified output (y,n,G(y)) satisfies ||G(y)+n||<=delta, return it. Otherwise, if R=D return Failure; else replace R by min(D,2R) and start a new trial from w. Never reuse a failed trial's unchecked center.
variants.requirements: T(G,w,mu,R,delta) has a finite schedule even for a false radius promise, accepts only a verified evaluated genuine normal certificate, and is guaranteed to succeed whenever R>=||w-zstar||. Standing model is specified in model_and_interfaces.
variants.state_and_initialization: rho=(mu/L_p)^(1/(p-1)); R=min(D,rho). Every trial initializes from the ORIGINAL point w.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Try min(D,2^j rho), j=0,1,..., without repeating D. The first valid radius succeeds; failure at D is impossible on a valid strong instance with the required trial.

variants.cost: At most two original queries per tensor iteration and two per final correction, allowing reuse when available. Per trial the scheduled cost is O_p(1+(L_p R^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))+log_+(A_p L_p R^p/delta)); this remains a schedule bound under false promises. Overall performance is Proposition 5.2, linked below.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Section 4 pp.11–15, equations (4.1)–(4.12), Algorithms 1–2; Proposition 5.2 p.16 and Algorithm 3 p.17.
variants.name: AdaptiveStrong(BaseTrial)
variants.output: An evaluated certificate (y,n,G(y)) with genuine original-domain normal and norm <=delta.
variants.query_and_update: While A_p L_p a^p>delta, replace z by Halve(G,z,mu,a), then a=a/2. Halve initializes x=z, Lambda=0 and s_avg=0, and runs T_p(a,mu)=max{1,ceil([2 b_p(4/3)^((p-1)/2)L_p a^(p-1)/mu]^(2/(p+1)))} iterations. Query the jet at x and solve 0 in Gbar_x(y)+beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x)+N_X(y), where Gbar_x(y)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}D^jG(x)[y-x]^j/j!. If y=x return y as an exact solution. Otherwise query G(y), set lambda=1/(beta||y-x||^(p-1)), accumulate s_avg+=lambda y and Lambda+=lambda, and set x=Pi_X(x-lambda G(y)). After the finite loop return s_avg/Lambda. After BaseTrial's halving loop, make one model correction at z: solve the same model for y, take n=-Gbar_z(y)-beta||y-z||^(p-1)(y-z), evaluate G(y), and accept only if ||G(y)+n||<=delta; otherwise return Failure.
variants.requirements: Standing strong model; exact projections and exact solutions of known regularized Taylor-model VIs are available as internal operations.
variants.state_and_initialization: Use the generic wrapper. Within each BaseTrial set z=w and a=R. Define b_p=2p/p!, beta=b_p L_p, A_p=(2p+1)3^p/p!.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: The halving and iteration schedules depend only on the guessed radius and public parameters. They remain finite under false promises. AdaptiveStrong doubles the radius only after a failed verified test, always restarting from w.

variants.cost: Every active ancestor counter is decremented before EACH original-F query, including all descendant queries. If a counter has no remaining allowance, interrupt its capped call immediately before the forbidden query and propagate failure; do not wait for an uncontrolled subcall to finish. Overall unknown-radius performance belongs to the composition in Lemma 5.3.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Definition 5.1 p.16; Lemma 5.3 and Algorithm 3 p.17; Algorithm 4 p.18.
variants.name: AdaptiveStrong(RestartTrial(A_{alpha,b}))
variants.output: Evaluated genuine normal certificate with norm <=delta.
public_inputs: Abstract capped A_{alpha,b} with known implementation constant
variants.query_and_update: At each trial stage set sigma=max(delta,mu a/2), call capped A(G,z,a,sigma), and immediately return Failure if it fails or its cap is exhausted. For verified (y,n,G(y)), return it when sigma=delta; otherwise set z=y and a=a/2 and continue. Full standalone trial record: alg.arxiv2609_13462.restart_trial.
variants.requirements: A_{alpha,b} satisfies Definition 5.1 including genuine evaluated certificates and interruptible nested caps. alpha>0 is fixed in the scope used by Lemma 5.3.
variants.state_and_initialization: Use the generic wrapper with T=RestartTrial; each trial initializes z=w and a=R.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Finite stage schedule for every radius guess; wrapper radii and original-anchor restarts follow the generic variant.

summary: Removes a supplied-distance promise using finite certified trials restarted from the original anchor. The BaseTrial and RestartTrial instantiations have distinct performance theorems; arbitrary trials have no generic complexity claim here.
title: AdaptiveStrong: certified geometric radius search
use_when: A finite certified trial succeeds for every valid supplied radius, but the actual distance to the strong VI solution is unknown.
